publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Prometheus and Drive

articleTitle: Improved obstacle detection by sensor fusion
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Prometheus and Drive
abstract: The authors describe recent work at Lucas in developing sensors and signal processing for collision avoidance. Results are presented that show the success of vehicle detection and lane marking detection using a video camera and a 94GHz microwave radar. Also discussed is research that is currently in progress that aims to combine the measurements from these sensors to give improved results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Traffic messaging, dynamic updating and road database standards: the major issues
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Prometheus and Drive
abstract: The authors describe how international efforts to develop and refine a standard for digital road databases (termed geographic data files (GDF)) have been paralleled by efforts to use traffic messages to update GDF, typically by RDS-TMC. The integration of RDS-TMC messages with GDF requires the resolution of some fundamental issues. These problems are being approached from different directions by PROMETHEUS and a number of DRIVE projects and findings are fed directly into CEN the European standards body, for early standardisation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Future applications for short range vehicle/roadside communications links
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Prometheus and Drive
abstract: The authors begin with a look at the way in which SRC links have developed and reached the market-place, and a representative system is briefly outlined. The authors continue by describing recent developments within PROMETHEUS and in particular within Jaguar's programme to exploit these links to bring road traffic information to drivers. The last part of the paper looks at the issues which will affect the development of these applications and determine those which will eventually become products.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Prometheus and Drive
abstract: Within the scope of the DRIVE & PROMETHEUS programs, there are many systems being developed to provide information to aid the driver. However, can the driver deal with all this additional information? Might this information, designed to aid the driver, be too much to cope with & so conversely be a hinderance, increasing the likelihood of accidents? The author describes how the ARIADNE project believes that there is a danger of driver information systems causing driver overload. It therefore is concerned with developing an intelligent driver interface to prevent such a situation arising.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Safe and effective mobility in Europe-the contribution of the PROMETHEUS programme
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Prometheus and Drive
abstract: The author describes the approach of the PROMETHEUS programme, which started in 1986 by an initiative of the automotive industry in the framework of the EUREKA platform, which is to consider vehicles as active elements integrated in road traffic and part of a whole transport system, which should be possible to optimize in terms of safety and efficiency. The basic concept is to establish the necessary links among the driver, the vehicle, the driving and traffic environment as well as the transport system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The socrates projects-progress towards a pan-European driver information system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Prometheus and Drive
abstract: The author briefly outlines the SOCRATES (system of cellular radio for traffic efficiency and safety) concept and introducing the four projects connected with the DRIVE 2 programme which are actively implementing the results of the DRIVE 1 SOCRATES project. This demonstrated that the concepts for a SOCRATES system were soundly based and that there were no technical obstacles in the path of full SOCRATES implementation. The main objective of each of the SOCRATES pilot projects is to speed up the process towards widespread commercial implementation of SOCRATES systems throughout Europe.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Driver's needs and response to traffic information
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Prometheus and Drive
abstract: The authors discuss the importance of assessment of driver response to traffic information, particularly variable message signs (VMS) used as an aid to route choice. They also describe how such assessments will be undertaken by the DRIVE II project QUO VADIS.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The DRIVE research projects PAMELA and ADEPT
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Prometheus and Drive
abstract: The authors describe the current work of the DRIVE II project ADEPT (automatic debiting and electronic payment for transport) which is continuing the development of the PAMELA automatic debiting transponder technology which began in the DRIVE I programme in 1989. The authors also describe the recent field trials of the PAMELA system in automatic debiting and in particular the automation of toll collection. Finally the plans for the ADEPT field trials in 5 separate European countries are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
